title: feat: opt-in HW acceleration for 2020 5K iMacs (Navi 14)
head: 38cba3980570
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The packaged mkinitcpio wrapper can turn a failed UKI build into a reported success
leads.consequence: When sudo resolves /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio, its wrapper drops the underlying /usr/bin/mkinitcpio status for non-preset calls. If mkinitcpio writes an image with .cmdline but reports builder errors or a failed post hook, the new check only verifies the two flags, copies that unsuccessful image, registers it, and prints success. With --default the user may boot an image whose initramfs/post-processing failed. Call /usr/bin/mkinitcpio explicitly and check its status before publishing; ensure the tests simulate a post-output nonzero status.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2); corroboration noted

leads.summary: A Limine template comment before the active default is replaced as if it were the default
leads.consequence: The first '^#?default_entry:' line may be Limine's documented '#default_entry: <OS name>/<kernel name>' template above 'default_entry: 2'. --default turns that comment into an active HW default but leaves the old active default below, saves the comment rather than the previous setting, and prints 'It is now the default'. A bootloader with two conflicting active defaults does not have the promised unique selection; the user's old explicit default remains. Match the active line first, replace only it, and test the upstream template shape.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q1: Limine uses first uncommented key; restore exact; Omarchy never produces that header

leads.summary: The custom pacman trigger misses multiple inputs whose updates regenerate the safe boot image
leads.consequence: The bundled upstream 90-mkinitcpio-install.hook also watches mkinitcpio-git, usr/src/*/dkms.conf, usr/lib/systemd/systemd, usr/bin/cryptsetup and usr/bin/lvm. Those transactions can rebuild the normal initramfs without matching this hook, leaving the installed HW image with stale initramfs contents; additionally upstream's usr/lib/modules/*/extramodules/ directory path differs from the PR's extramodules/* file glob. Mirror the upstream triggers or build the HW entry through the boot builder itself, and cover these targets in a hook fixture.

leads.summary: Removing linux-t2 leaves the separately named HW-acceleration boot entry behind
leads.consequence: The new hook has no linux-t2 Remove package operation and no usr/lib/modules/*/modules.builtin Remove path. Upstream's kernel-removal hook removes entries named linux-t2 and linux-t2-fallback, not the top-level imac20-hwaccel EFI entry. Removing the package can therefore leave the HW entry, its UKI and potentially its default_entry even though that kernel's modules have been removed; there is no subsequent transaction that necessarily invokes --rebuild to fall back. Trigger cleanup on kernel removal and test the default-entry path.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q2b: real but narrow (with --default, boots removed kernel until next rebuild)

leads.summary: Open PR #7309's repository-wide sed rule fails after these PRs merge
leads.consequence: #7309 adds test/shell.d/sed-follow-symlinks-test.sh, which rejects any bare sed -i in bin/ except three allowlisted files. This PR introduces three bare sed -i lines in the opt-in installer. The merged test exits 1 and reports all three; on symlinked limine.conf GNU sed -i also breaks the symlink and edits a copy instead of the intended target. Add --follow-symlinks to these calls. Both PRs are individually MERGEABLE against quattro, but their combined test does not pass.
leads.triage: factual, verified via gh (rule present in #7309 diff); dropped: merge-order detail for #7309, which also fails on existing base lines

leads.summary: Omarchy's config refresh removes the opt-in entry without removing its hook or EFI file
leads.consequence: After opt-in, omarchy-refresh-limine overwrites /boot/limine.conf with the shipped template and calls limine-update; neither invokes this custom pacman hook. The HW EFI file and hook remain, but its top-level entry and a chosen --default are gone. omarchy-reinstall-configs invokes this refresh too, so manual's 'run once after install' does not hold across normal reset/reinstall. Preserve or re-register the opt-in entry after refresh, or document the necessary reinstall command.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q2a: consistent and safe; re-added at next rebuild

leads.summary: Manual Limine rebuilds leave the custom image stale but the manual has no rerun instruction
leads.consequence: omarchy-hibernation-setup/remove and an explicit limine-mkinitcpio or limine-update rebuild the safe UKI/initramfs outside pacman. The optional HW UKI only rebuilds through its pacman hook or when the installer/--rebuild is invoked; the manual explains none of those after a manual rebuild. The bootable HW entry retains old cmdline/initramfs contents, potentially a stale resume target. Explain that rerunning omarchy-install-imac20-amdgpu-hwaccel after a manual Limine rebuild is required (or integrate into the rebuild path).

leads.summary: Open PR #10783 duplicates the 2020 iMac row if merged with this PR
leads.consequence: #10783 separately adds an A2115 iMac20,1/iMac20,2 row under the same T2 list, with slightly different wording. Its diff applies cleanly to this head and the combined Mac page contains two entries at lines 61 and 69. Coordinate the documentation change with #10783, retaining one row. #10783 is diverged, not stacked, and GitHub reports it MERGEABLE against the base.
leads.triage: factual, verified via gh; published after self-check wording fix F-4

leads.summary: An external Navi 14 GPU causes the safe display workaround to activate on a Navi 10 iMac
leads.consequence: The detector accepts any enumerated PCI display-class 1002:7340 on iMac20,*, not specifically the panel-driving internal GPU. An iMac20,2 with its internal Navi10 1002:7319 (the configuration of open PR #10169) and a Thunderbolt-connected Navi14 eGPU will be treated as affected. Install/migration then append nomodeset to the safe entry, removing acceleration from the otherwise different internal GPU, and the opt-in offers the Navi14 workaround unnecessarily. Check the internal GPU/subsystem identity or bus association instead of any GPU anywhere in sysfs.
leads.triage: first commit (unchanged, out of scope), niche; dropped

leads.summary: The entry tool can silently refuse --add-efi while the opt-in reports success
leads.consequence: If the copied HW UKI is under a non-FAT /boot (for example a user with an ESP mounted elsewhere, or a mistaken OMARCHY_UKI_DIR), LimineManager.addEfi returns false because getMountPointIfFat32 returns empty. Main.addEfi only saves when true and returns normally, so the CLI exit code is zero. The PR registers no menu entry but installs its hook and prints 'Added'; --default also points at an entry that does not exist. Check that the UKI path resides on the actual ESP and verify the registered entry after the call; a stub that only logs the invocation cannot catch this.
leads.triage: niche; Omarchy /boot is the ESP; dropped

leads.summary: The direct builder does not inherit configured UKI build options from the default image
leads.consequence: The packaged limine-mkinitcpio-install builder appends MKINITCPIO_UKI_OPTIONS to /usr/bin/mkinitcpio, including an explicitly supported --splash file. The new direct call passes only -k/-U/--cmdline, so the optional HW UKI differs from the safe image (e.g. has no configured boot splash), and subsequent --rebuilds keep dropping those options. Read and pass the validated UKI options from the same configured builder when constructing the alternate image, and test an optional option.
leads.triage: Opus: Omarchy sets none; dropped (REPORT only)

leads.summary: Migration records a completed repair even when the upstream kernel build was skipped
leads.consequence: The migration writes imac20-display.conf and then treats a zero exit from limine-mkinitcpio as proof that the safe image was rebuilt. Upstream's process_kernel suppresses a build_install_uki failure by returning zero and main loops with || true; it can return zero while leaving the old, unsafe image unchanged. The migration then writes its machine-wide repair marker and omarchy-migrate writes the user marker, so next login will not retry; on the affected hardware the LUKS display can still blank on next boot. Confirm the resulting safe UKI/entry cmdline before creating the marker, or change the upstream failure contract.
leads.triage: first commit, unchanged, out of scope; dropped

leads.summary: The opt-in command cannot follow the ESP remapping in open PR #7410
leads.consequence: #7410 migrates T2 overlays with a non-FAT /boot and a VFAT /boot/efi to ESP_PATH=/boot/efi and writes a regular linux-t2 entry there. With both branches applied, this installer still reads /boot/EFI/Linux/omarchy_linux-t2.efi and writes /boot/limine.conf, neither being the migrated ESP safe UKI/config. On an affected overlay the opt-in fails at the missing .cmdline (or writes outside the ESP if a stray file exists). Derive ESP_PATH and image format from Limine instead of hard-coding /boot. Only applies to the overlay installs #7410 supports, not stock installs.

leads.summary: Open PR #10169 conflicts at the same hardware registration line
leads.consequence: #10169 also inserts an iMac display workaround immediately after fix-t2.sh. Git merge-file with #10169's first parent as base places conflict markers at lines 37-41 of merged-10169-result.sh; even though both PRs are MERGEABLE against quattro individually, a merge of both requires resolving this hunk and keeping both independent steps. Their PCI predicates target different GPUs, so this is a textual integration conflict, not an incompatibility in their intended hardware behavior.
leads.triage: trivial conflict in unchanged first commit; dropped

leads.summary: Missing DMI product_name silently classifies the system as unrelated hardware
leads.consequence: Linux publishes /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name only when DMI_PRODUCT_NAME is non-null. If an affected 2020 iMac firmware/boot environment omits this field, the detector exits 1 with suppressed grep errors; both install and migration silently skip the safe display workaround, and the opt-in command says 'nothing to do' with exit 0. This is conditional, not a demonstrated iMac firmware state; settle by checking a real affected machine's DMI field or published SMBIOS table. Prefer a positive alternative identifier where possible and surface inability to identify this hardware rather than reporting an unrelated machine.

limits: No real iMac20 hardware, firmware boot, Secure Boot enrollment or host /boot experiment was performed; boot outcomes conditional on sources and isolated fixtures.

Kernel 7.2 / linux-t2 physical role of video=efifb:off remains unsettled: dep-kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c:2388 and dep-kernel/drivers/video/fbdev/efifb.c:376-379 establish code paths but not the user's panel outcome; hardware A/B boots would settle.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** after a typical `linux-t2` upgrade, the hook builds the HW-accel UKI from the old kernel.

Since the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12524#issuecomment-5858069193), at `38cba39`: failed-build, `--remove` and enrolled-config fixed; stale UKI partly; flags question closed.

### `--rebuild` uses the old kernel

`linux_t2_kernel` takes the first `linux-t2` `pkgbase`, but `kernel-modules-hook` restores the old kernel's directory first. **Impact:** the HW-accel entry boots the old kernel, whose modules go after one safe boot.

**Suggested change:** take `vmlinuz` from `pacman -Ql linux-t2`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 38cba39)</summary>

Append to `test/shell.d/imac20-amdgpu-hwaccel-test.sh` (it reuses the file's `run`, `$tmp_dir` and `$stubs`):

```bash
# During a linux-t2 upgrade, kernel-modules-hook (in Omarchy's base packages)
# copies the running kernel's module directory, pkgbase and vmlinuz included,
# back into /usr/lib/modules in its 10-linux-modules-post.hook, before the
# zz- hook runs. Only the new directory belongs to the linux-t2 package.
echo "iMac20,1" >"$tmp_dir/product_name"
old_kver=7.2.6-arch2-Watanare-T2-5-t2
new_kver=7.2.7-arch1-Watanare-T2-2-t2
rm -rf "$tmp_dir/modules"
for kver in "$old_kver" "$new_kver"; do
  mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/modules/$kver"
  echo linux-t2 >"$tmp_dir/modules/$kver/pkgbase"
  : >"$tmp_dir/modules/$kver/vmlinuz"
  : >"$tmp_dir/modules/$kver/modules.builtin"
done
cat >"$stubs/pacman" <<SH
#!/bin/bash
# linux-t2 owns only the upgraded kernel's directory.
case \$1 in
  -Ql) printf 'linux-t2 %s\n' "$tmp_dir/modules/$new_kver/"{pkgbase,vmlinuz,modules.builtin} ;;
  -Qqo) [[ \$2 == "$tmp_dir/modules/$new_kver/"* ]] && echo linux-t2 || exit 1 ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$stubs/pacman"

run || fail "opt-in succeeds after a linux-t2 upgrade" "$(cat "$tmp_dir/out.log")"
: >"$tmp_dir/calls.log"
run --rebuild || fail "--rebuild succeeds after a linux-t2 upgrade"
grep -Fq "mkinitcpio -k $tmp_dir/modules/$new_kver/vmlinuz " "$tmp_dir/calls.log" ||
  fail "rebuild after a linux-t2 upgrade builds the upgraded kernel" "$(grep '^mkinitcpio' "$tmp_dir/calls.log")"
pass "rebuild after a linux-t2 upgrade builds the upgraded kernel"
```

### `mkinitcpio` failures go undetected

`sudo mkinitcpio` runs the hook package's `/usr/local/bin` wrapper, which exits 0 for non-preset calls. **Impact:** a UKI that mkinitcpio reports as failed is installed and kept by `--rebuild`.

**Suggested change:** call `/usr/bin/mkinitcpio`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 38cba39)</summary>

On an Omarchy system with limine-mkinitcpio-hook, `mkinitcpio` resolves to the hook package's `/usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio`. This script runs the same failing call through the real binary and through the wrapper. It was run in a read-only sandbox on an Omarchy host with mkinitcpio 41.1, whose wrapper differs from the 1.40.0 file only in how the preset warning is printed (`echo -e` instead of `printf`). `data/limine-1.40.0-usr-local-bin-mkinitcpio` is `install/arch-linux/limine-mkinitcpio-hook/usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio` from limine-entry-tool tag 1.40.0.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Exit status of the installed mkinitcpio and of limine-mkinitcpio-hook's
# /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio wrapper for the same failing non-preset call.
# The kernel path does not exist, so mkinitcpio stops before reading any
# configuration or writing anything; the sandbox root is read-only.
set -uo pipefail
out=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$out"
here=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
echo "quiet nomodeset" >"$tmp/cmdline"

{
  for f in /usr/bin/mkinitcpio /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio; do
    if [[ -f $f ]]; then echo "present: $f"; else echo "missing: $f"; fi
  done
  if [[ -f /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio ]]; then
    echo "wrapper sha256: $(sha256sum </usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    echo "upstream 1.40.0 sha256: $(sha256sum <"$here/data/limine-1.40.0-usr-local-bin-mkinitcpio" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    cmp -s /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio "$here/data/limine-1.40.0-usr-local-bin-mkinitcpio" && echo "installed wrapper == upstream 1.40.0 file" || echo "installed wrapper differs from upstream 1.40.0 file"
  fi
  if [[ -x /usr/bin/mkinitcpio ]]; then
    echo "mkinitcpio version: $(/usr/bin/mkinitcpio --version 2>&1 | head -n1)"
    /usr/bin/mkinitcpio -k /nonexistent/vmlinuz -U "$tmp/hwaccel.efi" --cmdline "$tmp/cmdline" >"$out/direct.stdout" 2>"$out/direct.stderr"
    echo "/usr/bin/mkinitcpio exit: $?"
    echo "  stderr: $(tr '\n' ' ' <"$out/direct.stderr")"
  fi
  if [[ -x /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio ]]; then
    /usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio -k /nonexistent/vmlinuz -U "$tmp/hwaccel.efi" --cmdline "$tmp/cmdline" >"$out/wrapper.stdout" 2>"$out/wrapper.stderr"
    echo "/usr/local/bin/mkinitcpio exit: $?"
    echo "  stderr: $(tr '\n' ' ' <"$out/wrapper.stderr")"
    PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin
    echo "mkinitcpio resolved with Arch's default PATH: $(type -P mkinitcpio)"
  fi
  echo "UKI written: $([[ -e $tmp/hwaccel.efi ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
} 2>&1 | tee "$out/report.txt"
rm -rf "$tmp"
```
